name: Fourfold | Film Screening and Discussion
description:
A letter passes many hands over decades braving time, neglect and systems of care. Animated by stop motion, drawing, and erasure, personal letters and institutional archives merge, and transform into a shared public memory.

Meera K is an animation filmmaker from Bangalore, Karnataka with a focus on mixed media stop motion animation. She has directed and animated narrative shorts, non-fiction films, and title sequences. Her work explores the real and the imagined through the use of found objects, archives, and frame-by-frame drawings. She teaches animation as a visiting faculty at Srishti Manipal Institute of Technology. Her films have screened at festivals such as Animafest Zagreb, Animela Mumbai, and Sci560, among others.

**The film screening will be followed by a conversation with Paromita Vohra, filmmaker, writer, founder of Agents of Ishq, and the Obaid Siddiqi Chair for History and Culture of Science 2026-2027 at NCBS.**

**Friday, November 13, 2026. 5:00pm**

**Lecture Hall – 1 (Haapus), NCBS**

**2026 | Kannada, English, Hindi, Bengali with English subtitles**

**Length: 6 minutes 12 seconds**

name: Drawing Knowledge
description:
What can we learn about place and people from a detailed drawing?

This exhibition presents one of the largest private collections of architectural drawings of Rajasthan’s forts and palaces, from Jaisalmer and Amber to Mehrangarh and Hawa Mahal. Each drawing is the product of years of research and meticulous documentation, recording the walls, courtyards, and water systems that shaped life inside these buildings.

Comprehensive documentation of such places is increasingly scarce. Made possible by the mentorship of Kulbhushan Jain and Minakshi Jain, the collection brings this accumulated knowledge into the public domain. It gives researchers, students, and curious visitors access to study the details closely, now and for generations to come.

**Exhibition Opening:** 6:30pm, Fri, Nov 13

**Exhibition Timings:** 11am – 8pm | Fri, Nov 13 – Sun, Nov 15

**Exhibition on show until:** 8pm | Sun, Nov 15

**Walkthroughs:**

6:30pm | Fri, Nov 13

11am & 5:30pm | Sat, Nov 14

11am & 5:30pm | Sun, Nov 15

**Beyond the Lines | 7pm – 8:30pm | Fri, Nov 13**

A panel discussion exploring how architectural drawings of Rajasthan’s forts and palaces serve as archives of architectural, social and cultural knowledge, and their potential for future scholarship.

**Built Before the Blueprint Workshop | 11:30am – 1:30pm | Sat, Nov 14\***

A collaborative workshop inviting participants to read architectural drawings from the exhibition to discover how Rajasthan’s forts and palaces responded to their climate, resources, water needs and military strategies.

**Health, Heritage and Architecture Workshop | 6pm – 8pm | Nov 14\***

A workshop exploring how traditional architecture created cool, airy, bright and healthy spaces without electricity, using drawings from the exhibition.

name: Make your own Sashiko Bookmarks
description:
Japanese crafts are designed to be mindful, calming and skill-building, matching perfectly with our ethos at Knot Therapy.

Sashiko is an embroidery technique developed to preserve both garments and resources. Its unique style of using the minimum material by creating geometric patterns while reinforcing the fabric in such a way that it not only survives heavy use but the mending is decorative - the flaw becomes part of its beauty.

Join us to explore a brand new thread craft, some interesting history, make your very own bookmarks, all while learning a new technique to regulate yourself and make some calm with your own hands.

**What you get:**

4 sets of bookmarks to experiment with

Safe supplies to create the punch base

All tools & threads to create the embroidery

A guided and quiet experience, curated by your own pace & aesthetic.

**Open to Ages 16+**

name: Live Urban Sketching Bootcamp - Workshop Series
description:
*Learn how to draw on location and maintain a sketchbook with this 4 part live drawing bootcamp! Each session will begin with an instructional segment, learning an aspect of life drawing and building skills, followed by a live location demo and a practice session for participants. Instructional session will be conducted at Atta Galatta, Indiranagar, followed by the demo and drawing session at a different location in the area each week.*

*Each week we tackle something different -*

*Session 1 : Drawing Nature and Organic shapes.*

*Session 2 : Understanding Perspective and architecture.*

*Session 3: Drawing people.*

*Session 4: Capturing Light and Colour.*

*Dates : Saturdays, 9AM-12PM (3hrs) on 14th Nov, 21st Nov, 28th Nov & 5th December.*

Join us for the entire bootcamp or for a single session!
